reason: The stalk of a sporocarp (Marsilea, Azolla) is a stalk.
The peduncle of a sporocarp is its stalk, so this maps to stalk.
The pedicels of an umbellet are the flower stalks, so this maps to flower pedicel.
'Fall' means an outer tepal only in Iris and its relatives. Elsewhere it means leaf fall or the season, so the rule needs a flower or perianth context.
The endostome is the inner peristome of mosses, so its teeth are peristome teeth. The rule loses the inner/outer distinction, which is acceptable for a bearer.
Same word as 'disc gland', with a hyphen.
An epigynous gland is a nectary on top of an inferior ovary, which is an epigynous disc. It is not a general disc gland, and the match is doubtful, so reject it.
Throat scales are scales in the corolla throat, as in Boraginaceae. They are the same structure as faucal scales, which map to corolline corona.
Faucal scales (fornices) of the corolla throat map to corolline corona. The review of 2026-11-14 already said so.
The stalk of a leaflet is the petiolule.
'Areola' is an areole bud in cacti and Euphorbia. In leaf venation and in lichens it means a small area or space, so it must not be matched everywhere.
'Areole' is an areole bud in cacti. It also means the small area between veins in leaf venation.
The exostome is the outer peristome, and its teeth are the peristome teeth. 'Filament' is the term for the inner endostome processes, so this mixes the two rows. Reject it.
A green cell is a chlorophyll-bearing cell, which is a chlorenchyma cell (for example the chlorocysts in Sphagnum).
In sedges, spikelet scales are bracts that each subtend a flower, so flower bract fits. In grasses the glumes are not floral bracts.
This is the French form of 'spikelet scale'. It fits flower bract in sedges, but not for grass glumes.
Areolar glands of cacti are extrafloral nectaries.
Areole glands of cacti are extrafloral nectaries.
The culm is the stem of a grass or sedge, so a culm internode is a stem internode.
Plural of 'culm internode'.
A nucule is a small nut. It is a mericarp only in schizocarpic fruits such as Boraginaceae and Lamiaceae. In Chara it is the oogonium.
Plural of 'nucule'. The same limits apply: it is a mericarp only in schizocarpic fruits.
Sclerotic granules are small groups of stone cells. Sclerenchyma is the whole tissue, so the mapping loses the 'cluster' part of the meaning. It is acceptable only as a loose approximation.
Singular of 'sclerotic granule'. A granule is a cluster of stone cells, not the tissue, so the same limit applies.
Stone cells are sclereids, which are sclerenchyma. A cluster of them is a portion of sclerenchyma.
Grit cells are stone cells (sclereids), so a cluster of them is a portion of sclerenchyma.

'Lip' is either the orchid labellum or a corolla lip. The lip class (FLOPO_0985017) fits the corolla lip. Labellum lobe fits only when the part is an orchid labellum, as the 'lip limb' rejection shows.
A branchlet of an inflorescence is a higher-order inflorescence axis.
This is the same as 'inflorescence branchlet', written the other way round.
A cell of the central strand is a cell, not the strand. Mapping it to central strand loses the 'cell' part.
A bract-like sheath is a sheath, not a scale leaf. A bract-like sheath is not a cataphyll.
A sheathing bract is a bract, not a scale leaf (cataphyll). It should map to bract.
A sterile bract is a bract that bears no flower. It is not a scale leaf, so it should map to bract.
'Fruited' is an adjective meaning 'bearing fruit' or 'in fruit'. It is a state of the plant, not a part, so it is not a bearer.
Transverse veins join the secondary veins, which makes them tertiary veins. 'Cross-vein' is already a PO synonym.
An anthelodium is an anthela-type inflorescence (Juncaceae, Cyperaceae).
Same word as 'leaf scar', with a hyphen.
A lobe of the flower is a lobe of its perianth, so it maps to perianth lobe.
'Punctation' means a pattern of dots or pits. It is a quality (punctate), not a secretory tissue.
A costula is the secondary rachis (midrib) of a pinnule in ferns, not a vascular bundle. No existing class fits, so reject it.
A primary pinnule is a pinnule. The rank is lost but the part is the same.
The stipe of a tegula is a stalk. Low confidence, because 'tegula' is a rare word.
Epicalyx scales are the bracts of the epicalyx.
Plural of 'epicalyx scale'.
A stem leaf is a cauline leaf.
A stem leaf is a cauline leaf.
Plural of 'stem-leaf', which is a cauline leaf.
Plural of 'stem leaf', which is a cauline leaf.
Perianth scales are reduced tepals, as in Cyperaceae and Juncaceae.
Plural of 'perianth scale', which is a reduced tepal.
